Phoenix Education Partners, Inc. completed an initial public offering in which selling stockholders affiliated with Apollo and Vistria sold 4,887,500 shares of common stock at $32.00 per share for an aggregate offering price of $156.4 million, with the company receiving no proceeds.
The company paid a $12.2 million fee in fiscal year 2025 to terminate its strategic transaction with Four Three Education, Inc.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Phoenix Education Partners, Inc. operates through its subsidiary The University of Phoenix, Inc. to provide online post-secondary higher education to working adults in the United States.
quotes: We, through our subsidiary The University of Phoenix, Inc., are a pioneer of online higher education for working adults in the United States.
Our student body, which consists primarily of working adult learners seeking to advance their careers, represents an attractive and growing sub-segment of the higher education market.

business_model.claim: The University sells degree-granting programs across disciplines including business, IT, health professions, social and behavioral sciences, education, nursing, doctoral studies, and general studies, representing approximately 98% of net revenue in fiscal year 2026.
quotes: The University currently offers a number of degree-granting and non-degree certificate programs across a wide range of disciplines, including business and information technology (“IT”), health professions, social and behavioral sciences, education, nursing, doctoral studies, and general studies.
Our degree-granting programs represented approximately 98% of our net revenue for fiscal year 2026 and serve a diverse set of students who are seeking to improve their career opportunities:

business_model.claim: In fiscal year 2026, Average Total Degreed Enrollment of 83,700 comprised 67,400 undergraduate and 16,300 graduate students across Bachelor's (70%), Master's (17%), Associate's (10%), and Doctoral (3%) programs.
quotes: For the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, the University’s Average Total Degreed Enrollment was 83,700, including 67,400 undergraduate and 16,300 graduate students.
Bachelor’s: 70%

business_model.claim: During fiscal year 2026, 73% of enrolled students were currently employed, 94% of new students were over age 22 with an average age of 37, 72% were female, and 53% were first-generation college students.
quotes: 73% are currently employed;
94% of new students are over the age of 22, with an average age of 37;

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P8
business_model.claim: Beyond degrees, the company sells shorter credit-bearing certificates and non-credit professional development courses and is expanding into talent-sourcing and AI-powered workforce intelligence through its acquisition of Fuel50 Inc.
quotes: These non-degree offerings include shorter credit-bearing certificates and non-credit professional development courses designed to provide flexible options for working adults to develop critical skills for career advancement.
On September 30, 2026, we acquired all of the outstanding stock of Fuel50 Inc. (“Fuel50”), an AI-powered workforce intelligence platform.

business_model.claim: Students enroll either independently or through B2B employer relationships that provide discounted tuition benefits and represented 35.2% of Average Total Degreed Enrollment in fiscal year 2026, up 3.2 percentage points from fiscal year 2025.
quotes: Many of our students receive discounted tuition benefits under programs offered through our employer relationships, which are classified as B2B enrollment.

Enrollment through our employer relationships represented 35.2% of our Average Total Degreed Enrollment in fiscal year 2026, which represents a 3.2 percentage point increase compared to fiscal year 2025.

business_model.claim: Under its non-term academic delivery model, students take consecutive courses and net revenue is recognized evenly over each course's duration, excluding holiday breaks.
quotes: Under the University’s non-term academic delivery model, students generally enroll in a program of study encompassing a series of courses taken consecutively over the length of the program, and net revenue is recognized evenly over the duration of the course (e.g., daily over five weeks for a five-week course, other than the University’s holiday breaks when no related net revenue is recognized).

business_model.claim: Most annual consolidated net revenue comes from Title IV federal student financial aid disbursed to students, with 88.6% of cash basis revenue in the most recent fiscal year derived from Title IV and other designated federal education assistance funds.
quotes: Most of our annual consolidated net revenue is derived from the receipt of Title IV program funds disbursed to our students.

we derived 88.6% of our cash basis revenue from Title IV and other designated federal education assistance funds in our most recent fiscal year, and if the University becomes ineligible to participate in Title IV programs, including due to the “90/10 Rule,” or participation is materially limited, our business may not be sustainable;

business_model.claim: Net revenue depends largely on total courses taken and price per course, rising 1.0% to $1,016,969 (table in thousands) in fiscal year 2026 from $1,007,192 (table in thousands) in fiscal year 2025 as Average Total Degreed Enrollment grew 2.2%.
quotes: The net revenue we generate in a given period largely depends on the total number of courses taken by the enrolled student population and the price per course.
Net revenue increased $9.8 million, or 1.0%, in fiscal year 2026 compared to fiscal year 2025.

business_model.claim: Improved undergraduate student retention, which increased from 59.7% for the 2016/2017 cohort to 76.6% for the 2024/2025 cohort, has been a key driver of recent enrollment growth.
quotes: Our student retention rates, calculated as (i) the number of confirmed undergraduate students who both started a degree or non-degree certificate program and posted attendance in a course within such program as of an applicable date, divided by (ii) the number of confirmed undergraduate students who started such a program, expressed as a percentage, have increased from 59.7% for the 2016/2017 cohort to 76.6% for the 2024/2025 cohort (our most recent completed cohort for retention rate purposes), which represents a 5.1 percentage point increase from the 2023/2024 cohort.
The increase in retention is a key factor driving the growth in Average Total Degreed Enrollment in recent years, including a 2.2% increase in fiscal year 2026 as compared to fiscal year 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P3
business_model.claim: Tuition rates were held flat from 2018 through fiscal year 2026 before tuition increases for new students were implemented on November 2, 2026, while Tuition Price Guarantee and Locked-In Pricing Guarantee fix prices for continuing eligible students.
quotes: As part of our focus on affordable and accessible tuition, we did not increase tuition rates from 2018 through fiscal year 2026.

On November 2, 2026, we implemented tuition rate increases for new students and introduced the Locked-In Pricing Guarantee, which provides new students with a combined per-course price covering both tuition and the resource fee that remains fixed from enrollment through graduation in their enrolled program.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P3
business_model.claim: Enrollment and revenue are influenced by student discovery behavior, including through AI-enabled platforms, and by increasing competition in online distance education from traditional colleges and universities.
quotes: Recently, enrollment has been influenced in part by changes in prospective student search and discovery behavior, including through AI-enabled platforms.

While we are one of the largest universities in the U.S. that predominantly focuses on the distance education market (defined as universities with 90% or more of students enrolled in distance education) according to the Department of Education’s National Center for Education Statistics, no single institution has a significant share of the total post-secondary market.

business_model.claim: Instructional and support is the largest cost category at 440,029 (table in thousands), or 43.3% of net revenue, in fiscal year 2026, driven by faculty and student-facing staff compensation, credit losses on accounts receivable, financial aid processing, course development, and depreciation.
quotes: Instructional and support principally consists of costs related to the delivery and administration of our educational programs and includes compensation and related costs (including share-based compensation) for faculty, academic administrators, enrollment and student advisory personnel, credit losses associated with uncollectible accounts receivable, financial aid processing costs and depreciation of applicable property and equipment.
Instructional and support increased $4.0 million, or 0.9%, in fiscal year 2026 compared to fiscal year 2025, and remained flat as a percentage of net revenue at 43.3%.

business_model.claim: General and administrative expenses totaled 408,619 (table in thousands), or 40.2% of net revenue, in fiscal year 2026, up from 352,634 (table in thousands), or 35.0%, in fiscal year 2025, driven by administrative compensation, advertising, IT infrastructure, legal and professional fees, and corporate facility rent.
quotes: General and administrative principally consists of compensation and related costs (including share-based compensation) for management and employees in administrative functions, advertising expense, legal and professional fees, information technology infrastructure costs, depreciation of property and equipment associated with our administrative functions, rent and related expenses associated with our corporate facilities and other related costs.
General and administrative increased $56.0 million, or 15.9%, in fiscal year 2026 compared to fiscal year 2025, and increased as a percentage of net revenue from 35.0% to 40.2%.

business_model.claim: Strategic alternatives, restructuring and other expenses were 45,660 (table in thousands), or 4.5% of net revenue, in fiscal year 2026, reflecting capital market transaction costs, net lease expense on exited space, cybersecurity incident costs, and litigation and regulatory expenses.
quotes: Strategic alternatives, restructuring and other principally consists of (1) costs associated with exploring and executing strategic alternative and capital market transactions, (2) net lease expense for space we have exited, (3) expense associated with the cybersecurity incident detected in November 2025, including the estimated loss contingency associated with the related class action litigation, (4) certain litigation and regulatory expenses, and (5) other items that we consider unusual or infrequent.

business_model.claim: Margin expansion has historically relied on operating leverage over largely fixed costs and exiting all ground campuses except one, supplemented after fiscal year 2026 by voluntary and involuntary workforce reductions.
quotes: Our margin expansion over recent years has been largely derived from the operating leverage resulting from the increase in net revenue relative to our costs that are more fixed in nature and our exit from all but one of our ground campuses.
Subsequent to August 31, 2026, we implemented a voluntary separation program and initiated separate involuntary workforce reductions as we continue to manage our cost structure.

The increase in retention is a key factor driving the growth in Average Total Degreed Enrollment in recent years, including a 2.2% increase in fiscal year 2026 as compared to fiscal year 2025.

Although we continue to adapt our marketing and enrollment strategies, these changes may affect the timing and pace at which prospective students engage with the University and make enrollment decisions and impact the effectiveness of our enrollment process.
